item.description: Because of its outstanding strength and other physical properties, Master Bond Supreme 10HT has been selected for use in several published research studies. Following are summaries of how Supreme 10HT performed in demanding applications outlined in these studies.

item.title: Artificial Tendons Give Muscle-Powered Robots a Boost
item.description: Our muscles are nature’s actuators. The sinewy tissue is what generates the forces that make our bodies move. In recent years, engineers have used real muscle tissue to actuate “biohybrid robots” made from both living tissue and synthetic parts. By pairing lab-grown muscles with synthetic skeletons, researchers are engineering a menagerie of muscle-powered crawlers, walkers, swimmers, and grippers.

item.title: This AI Can Predict Future X-Rays
item.description: An AI system that can predict what a patient’s knee X-ray will look like a year in the future could transform how millions of people with osteoarthritis understand and manage their condition, according to research by the University of Surrey.

item.title: How Much Do You Know About the History of Military Drones?
item.description: Military drones have evolved from early experimental concepts into indispensable assets on today’s battlefield. From surveillance to precision strikes, their rapid technological advancement has reshaped how modern militaries operate.

item.title: Greener Energy? Drinkable Seawater? This Sodium-Ion Battery Breakthrough May Deliver Just that
item.description: Unlike lithium-ion technology, which currently dominates the energy storage market and relies on expensive, environmentally damaging materials, sodium is far more abundant and widely available. However, developing sodium-ion batteries that can compete on performance has remained a challenge.

item.title: Microscopic Swimming Machines that Can Sense, Respond to Surroundings
item.description: Researchers at the University of Pennsylvania and University of Michigan have created the world’s smallest fully programmable, autonomous robots: microscopic swimming machines that can independently sense and respond to their surroundings, operate for months, and cost just a penny each.

item.title: Powering America’s EV Future: Connect, Collaborate, Innovate
item.description: Since 2021, the U.S. has made remarkable strides in EV charging infrastructure — but the journey is far from complete. The past year’s policy changes have brought both opportunities and uncertainty, making collaboration more important than ever.

item.title: Small Actuator Selection Guide
item.description: From packaging to life science applications to office equipment to factory automation, smooth motion, fast accelerating and highly accurate are hallmarks of high quality linear movement actuators. Together with increasing needs for miniaturization, actuators must also be compact. One system that meets both requirements in its conversion of motor torque to linear thrust is the single axis ball screw actuator.

item.title: Next-Generation Linear and Rotary Stages: When Ultra Precision Movement Is a Must
item.description: Achieving advanced, modern motion performance often feels like a battle against physics. Designers face tradeoffs among speed, precision, and cost, while real-world effects like thermal drift, vibration, geometric errors, and tolerance stackups can result in diminished performance.
